facts.statement: The researchers used a large cohort study design that combined data from 42,039 people in two major databases.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study measured white matter free water using diffusion MRI to track extracellular water levels and tissue microstructure.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Genetic analysis found 27 specific gene locations linked to white matter free water and highlighted 88 genes for further study.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study found that both inherited genetic risks and actual MRI measurements of white matter water were linked to various neurological conditions.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Higher levels of white matter free water on scans were strongly connected to stroke and dementia.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People with higher initial levels of white matter free water were more likely to progress from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Special genetic analysis suggested a two-way link between high blood pressure and white matter free water levels.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Protein analysis identified two specific proteins that might explain how blood pressure affects white matter water levels.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors conclude that white matter free water is a useful imaging marker for assessing genetic and vascular risks for neurological disorders.
facts.subject: humans
